Updated [GitHub reporting](/home/maxwell-rosen/gkeyll/ci/jenkins/github_report.py) to exclude warnings originating in any `ker/` directory from warning lists, counts, and baseline comparisons. Kernel errors and raw logs remain available. All 25 reporting tests pass.

The report contains **214 occurrences across baseline and candidate builds**, not 214 distinct problems:

| Warning | Count | Recommendation |
|---|---:|---|
| NaN/infinity with fast-math | 191 | **Investigate; don’t globally suppress.** |
| Discarded `const` qualifiers | 16 | **Fix:** eight source locations reported twice. |
| Density selection clamped to available data | 4 | Ignore only where the test intentionally exercises this fallback. |
| Compiler summaries / garbled output | 3 | Reporting noise. |

**Fast-math is the substantive issue.** The Makefile enables `-ffast-math`, while functions use `isnan` and `isfinite` for correctness checks. These compiler assumptions can invalidate those checks. Trying `-fno-finite-math-only` after `-ffast-math` is a small configuration change, but needs numerical and performance verification. Merely disabling the warning won’t fix the behavior. [Clang documentation](https://clang.llvm.org/docs/UsersManual.html)

**The `const` warnings are mostly straightforward cleanup** in `core/zero/util.c`: copy into mutable temporary pointers before storing them, make getter types consistent, and clarify ownership for deallocation. Avoid blanket casts that conceal ownership mistakes.

**The six “new” warnings appear contaminated by interleaved build output**, including an existing warning with `mkdir` appended. GNU Make output synchronization would address this reporting problem.

One limitation: the supplied log has damaged source locations. The filter removes 158 identifiable kernel diagnostics from that report; ambiguous, garbled diagnostics remain visible rather than risking suppression of unrelated warnings.
